title: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: library for efficient training, model development and simulation of molecular systems
experiments_summary: Three MLIP models (MACE, NequIP, ViSNet) were implemented in JAX and pre-trained on a curated version of the SPICE2 dataset (~1.74M training structures, ~88K validation structures, 15 chemical elements), split 95:5 at the SMILES level to prevent conformer leakage. Each model was trained for 220 epochs on NVIDIA H100 GPUs; ViSNet and NequIP used Huber loss, MACE used MSE loss. MACE was trained under two hyperparameter configurations: a 'large' variant (2 layers, 128 channels, correlation order 2, max L=3) prioritizing MD stability, and a 'medium' variant following MACE-OFF hyperparameters. MACE was also trained on a curated SPICE1 dataset with MACE-OFF medium hyperparameters for comparison. A modified MACE architecture was developed with two architectural changes—species-dependent gating of node features using scalars from the Symmetric Contraction, and species-dependent edge interaction weights built from sender/receiver species embeddings—aimed at improving inference speed without sacrificing accuracy. Validation was performed by computing mean absolute error (MAE) for energy per atom (meV/atom) and atomic forces (meV/Å) across seven SPICE2 subsets covering isolated and solvated small molecules. Runtime benchmarks were conducted by running 1-nanosecond MD simulations on two protein systems (1UAO and 1ABT) and comparing simulation speeds between the JAX+JAX-MD and Torch+ASE backends, with results averaged over the full simulation. Padding strategies for neighbor lists were applied in both backends to minimize JAX recompilation overhead.
